glasshouse.name: The Glasshouse
glasshouse.idea: One building where eggs and plants share everything. Blackthorn sits against the Ice Path, so both need heat, and the heat comes from Pokémon. A Magcargo hearth at the core keeps the eggs warm; the greenhouse rings wrap around it and live on the same heat. Ampharos lights both through the winter. Eggs hatch by being walked, so the walk that hatches them runs through the crop rows: the egg walk is the harvest walk.

decisions.title: PKHeX
decisions.text: Zack has PKHeX and can create and import custom Pokémon

decisions.title: Learnability standard.
decisions.text: Learnability standard. "I don't care if PKHeX says it's legal or not — it's legal in the sense that it can be learned and that's what fits my narrative… I'm not entering competitions, I'm creating the world I want." A move is valid for this project if the species can learn it. PKHeX legality, encounter/ball/origin constraints, egg-move-on-starter conflicts and save-plausibility do not gate canon; the engine reports them as story notes only. Example: HeartGold's Typhlosion can be Elm's starter and know Extrasensory. Open boundary: "learnable in that game" vs "learnable by the species in any game" (Q5)

decisions.title: Project home is Google Drive
decisions.text: Project home is Google Drive (Gen 1–4 scope keeps it manageable). Canon data lives in a Google Sheet that Claude reads and writes through the Sheets connector; docs live in a Drive project folder

decisions.title: HM/field rule kept as the ideal; every game gets worked through explicitly
decisions.text: HM/field rule kept as the ideal; every game gets worked through explicitly, with principled exceptions allowed where there's a real reason ("I don't hate the rule, I just want to work through it")

decisions.text: F4: revisit Platinum's Waterfall (and Defog), both lost when Lucario replaced the January roster's Empoleon

decisions.title: Product scope: a lab and workbench at PKHeX parity.
decisions.text: Product scope: a lab and workbench at PKHeX parity. Build teams, and build each individual as a battler and as breeding stock, down to ball, held item, IVs, EVs and every lever PKHeX exposes. Show what each choice causes (e.g. IVs and nature → summary-screen text). Everything exports into PKHeX so it's real

decisions.title: Build order: engines before specifics.
decisions.text: Build order: engines before specifics. Battle opponents (benchmarks), the authored world, and multi-generation breeding were built first ("I want 1, 2 and 3 right now, or at least begin the engines they'll need")

decisions.title: Approved all 15 HeartGold world records (W-001…W-015)
decisions.text: Approved all 15 HeartGold world records (W-001…W-015): the handoff §10 life roles mapped to capabilities ("approve all 15")

decisions.title: Camp life:
decisions.text: Camp life: food and cooking "could be any… it depends on the team" (berries, Apricorns, actual cooking). Build a camp-life portion; "not really a massive priority"

decisions.title: Endgame vision: a Champion's breeding ranch.
decisions.text: Endgame vision: a Champion's breeding ranch. Town life is reframed: "think of it more like end game is a breeding ranch… for a Pokémon champion with unlimited money, with unlimited land in as many places, regions 1–4, and obviously with the power of Pokémon… that's kind of a big goal of this too."

decisions.title: One headquarters
decisions.text: One headquarters ("one headquarters"). Satellites only where the headquarters can't give a resident its land. Location still a proposal (Blackthorn highlands)

decisions.title: Companions' fates stay open
decisions.text: Companions' fates stay open ("let's leave it open so we can say any of those"): retire to the ranch, stay with family, go back to the wild, or go with the rival. The census counts every companion as a possible resident

decisions.title: Breeding stock: build the lineage, keep only the final product
decisions.text: Breeding stock: build the lineage, keep only the final product ("you want to essentially build the lineage but you're only keeping the final breeding stock product"). Working reading: one male of each target line who knows the whole egg-move set (a stud, so every future egg is one step); the fathers used along the way aren't kept; a held-item line (Volt Tackle) keeps the Light Ball

decisions.title: Ranch staff: both Pokémon and people
decisions.text: Ranch staff: both Pokémon and people ("both"). Pokémon jobs come from game-backed or authored capabilities; people roles (head breeder, Day-Care keepers, nurse, cook, ranch hands, wardens, archivist) are placeholders to author

decisions.title: Ranch access: private, with an open Day-Care.
decisions.text: Ranch access: private, with an open Day-Care. "Think of it like the day care center gazillionaire edition in the sense of its open. But not all of it is open because the day care is just like a feature of it… it's super exclusive, it's not massive, think more wildlife preserve with daycare aspect for that portion of it." The scale note applies to the Day-Care and public side only, not to the whole ranch

decisions.title: Headquarters: Blackthorn
decisions.text: Headquarters: Blackthorn ("Blackthorn is an excellent answer"). Next: a hatchery woven into a greenhouse, designed from scratch for that site (proposal: The Glasshouse, `ranch.json` designs)

decisions.title: Past-tense frame:
decisions.text: Past-tense frame: "think of this all written in the past tense… all of these Pokémon are retired and that's where this whole breeding ranch is like the centerpiece." The journey is over; the present is a retired Champion's breeding ranch. Where each companion lives stays open (D-037)

decisions.title: Battle = scouting reports and call sheets, not simulations.
decisions.text: Battle = scouting reports and call sheets, not simulations. The teams are "the teams I could have used on my journey", like asking what Ash could have done with all his Pokémon at their peak. "Imagine creating scouting reports with tendencies… a Major League Baseball scouting report or an NFL call sheet… that's where I like having all of this data… with Smogon." Engine: `battle/scouting.py` (20–80 tool grades, present/peak, tendencies, splits, comps; call sheets from the benchmark grid)

decisions.title: The breeding lab is the present, and the journey is one family tree.
decisions.text: The breeding lab is the present, and the journey is one family tree. "I'm a breeder now, a retired champion, and the thing I do is tinker with different builds and trying to achieve different move sets and breeding stock that can go different ways. In a certain sense every single Pokémon part of the journey should be either a parent to a breeding stock or the product of breeding stock… and then even more Pokémon that weren't necessarily part of my journey but could be part of others." Engine: `breeding/studbook.py`; the lab runs on Gen 4 rules (HGSS + Platinum, Gen 3 by Pal Park) as a working choice

decisions.title: The Glasshouse is approved
decisions.text: The Glasshouse is approved ("approve the glasshouse"): the hatchery and greenhouse in one building at Blackthorn, with the hatching loop and the cold vault. Its two story-only jobs are proposed as W-016 (Meganium, plant care) and W-017 (Miltank, food source)

decisions.title: Scouting reports carry no grades: tendencies, philosophies, and how to attack.
decisions.text: Scouting reports carry no grades: tendencies, philosophies, and how to attack. "I don't want grades. More tendencies. And like philosophies. And how to attack them based on their moves and Pokémon, maybe order, or what they'll do when they're behind or ahead or against certain types or certain moves… combine the knowledge from the data and make it intelligent and customizable, and certain numbers triggering certain phrases, the same way it happens in the game." Engine: an editable phrase book where data thresholds trigger phrases; opponents' behavior comes from the games' own trainer AI flags, items and battle messages

decisions.title: The scouting engine is built, not tuned to an answer.
decisions.text: The scouting engine is built, not tuned to an answer. "I don't want you to design it around an answer, I want you to design the engine… and then have the lab so that we can use that engine… combine moves and what they do and damage and how movesets and type coverage and Smogon suggested movesets work." The engine (`docs/SCOUTING_ENGINE.md`) reads each move's plays from data, measures every team against what real players ran (Smogon's MIT usage sets), plays each one-on-one out as a measurement, and turns the results into sliders, play sheets and game plans. It keeps D-043: the product is still scouting reports and call sheets; the one-on-ones are the measuring stick, not a simulated six-on-six. The slider definitions, the situations and the peak defaults (IVs 31, EVs 85 in every stat) are WORKING proposals, open for argument; coach settings stay empty until you set them

decisions.title: Move legality is biological.
decisions.text: Move legality is biological. "I'd very much treat the whole move legality as almost a biological thing where it's like are they physically capable of doing it, and if they are I'm mostly good with it. It's my world and I want it to be true, but ultimately I make the rules, and if I want something to be true and there's some sort of reason, I think we can allow it." A move counts if the species (or a pre-evolution) can learn it in any game of any generation, uses it in the show, or the build records a reason. The report states the reason (e.g. "learns it in Crystal (machine)"). Only a move with no reason at all is flagged. Settles Q5

decisions.title: The project learns through one intake: cards of proposed claims, approved before they land.
decisions.text: The project learns through one intake: cards of proposed claims, approved before they land. "I just want to make sure we're utilizing all of our previous tools to be able to ingest as much information as possible so this project continues to grow and get smarter." Videos, screenshots, pages, pastes and research become cards; nothing reaches canon unapproved; every claim keeps its source. Videos run on Gemini in Food OS's envelope format. "At the end of the day, we probably end up with a separate sheet and engine that all TikToks or IG Reel videos for all of these different sources goes and then gets run, but we can build separate for now." So: built separately for Pokémon now (`engine/ingest/`, `docs/INGEST.md`, the Pokémon Master OS Agent Sheet), shaped so a shared engine can take it over
decisions.status: LOCKED (direction) · approval default: everything through Zack

decisions.title: Game film: Showdown replays, read exactly, are how the project learns real play.
decisions.text: Game film: Showdown replays, read exactly, are how the project learns real play. "Pay attention to the Pokémon and the builds and the order and obviously just learn as much as possible." The film room reads every replay turn by turn (no model, no cost): the order teams come in, each Pokémon's build as revealed and its move order, every choice with the game state before it. Studies of a player or a field become cards of observation tallies and build variants; approved ones show on the playsheet as On film. Game trainers send their party in order and mark their ace by level, so a cartridge team's unique top-level member is its derived ace (Lance's Lv 50 Dragonite, sent last)

decisions.title: Bulbapedia answers the open questions from its page source, read exactly first; the games' Pokédex backs or doesn't back what videos claim.
decisions.text: Bulbapedia answers the open questions from its page source, read exactly first; the games' Pokédex backs or doesn't back what videos claim. Moves-used tables, trainer entries and Achievements lists are structured, so they're parsed, not summarized; the model reads only prose (a moveset's moment, an anime ace) and its answers are cached. A moveset keeps every move the page supports and only replaces what it doesn't. Order sentences give a rival's send-out order for their defining battle. Every answer is a correction or observation for review, citing its page

decisions.title: The ladder's monthly numbers fill what film can't show.
decisions.text: The ladder's monthly numbers fill what film can't show. Smogon's monthly stats give each Pokémon's spreads, items, moves, teammates and checks. A film build is proposed the field spread that fits its role best (the role engine scores each top spread on the build). Every playsheet shows what beats each member on the ladder for its generation. Replays and stats stay reference data; only reviewed corrections land

decisions.title: The engine is held to outside references, and a wrong line in a report becomes a check.
decisions.text: The engine is held to outside references, and a wrong line in a report becomes a check. "I saw one of the examples you gave say Snorlax wasn't bulky - I just want to make sure the engine isn't awful." `engine/sanity.py` checks the stat formula against Smogon's calc for every fully evolved Pokémon of Gens 2-4, every library build, trainer team and builds book set against the games' data, every cached replay against the protocol's own rules, and our reading of Smogon's numbers against the file Smogon prints. Known facts live in `engine/sanity.json`; when a report says something wrong, the fact is added there before the code is fixed, so it can't come back. Softness is measured against the field with HP counted; Gen 2 builds use Gen 2's stat system (docs/SANITY.md, E-037 to E-040)

decisions.title: Blackthorn gets its Canon DB Sheet, with a lineage tracker and an Apps Script.
decisions.text: Blackthorn gets its Canon DB Sheet, with a lineage tracker and an Apps Script. "Are we forgetting that this is just the battling component of this project? Can we build out the whole Blackthorn base / dashboard and breeding stock program and lineage tracker and then do what we set out to do and put this all in a beautifully presented Google Sheet / app script." The Sheet (D-025) opens on a Blackthorn dashboard and holds the journey, the census, facilities, the Glasshouse, the breeding program, the studbook, pedigrees, fathers, your calls, the ledger, evidence, locks and the world records. The lineage tracker follows individuals: founders, the planned pedigree derived from D-038, and authored records in canon/lineage.json, checked against Gen 4's breeding rules. Derived tabs are rebuilt by the engine; what you type is authored and reaches canon when you say so. The Apps Script adds the Blackthorn menu (lineage tree, record a hatch, check the studbook) and a guard on locked rows (docs/BLACKTHORN.md)

decisions.title: Blackthorn HQ: one web app over the Sheet, the engines and the documents.
decisions.text: Blackthorn HQ: one web app over the Sheet, the engines and the documents. "Build an app using Google Sheets and the Apps Script and the web app. It should contain all of this - from the battle and trainer scouting engine to the breeding stock and lineage tracker to the lab to the glasshouse." Art direction is Zack's "Pokémon Heritage Solarpunk" (charcoal, gold, ivory, forest, ice, ember; type colors intact): "Luxury in presentation. Science in structure. Pokémon in identity. Life in every environment." Honesty rule, verbatim: "Measurements should be backed by real entered or simulated data, never presented as verified live readings without a data source." The app (engine/app) is served by an Apps Script web app (appscript/WebApp.gs, only Zack can open it) from one zip on Drive; it reads the engine's exports and the Sheet, and writes only its own log tabs, hatches to the Studbook and answers to Your Calls, each logged on the Timeline. An answer becomes a decision only when it's written into canon (docs/APP.md)

decisions.title: The app is a lab: the engines you tinker with run in the browser, held to Python by tests.
decisions.text: The app is a lab: the engines you tinker with run in the browser, held to Python by tests. "Make sure all of the scouting report mechanics and everything are incorporated as well, I want to be able to use this web app like a lab where I can tinker with values and see how they affect writeups... create whatever sections in this web app that you need so that... the whole project that we talked about from the start happens as best we have it right now so that we can see where we need to work on it." The trainer report engine (report, matrix, sliders, roles, playsheet, exposure), the wilderness engine and the specimen kernel are ported to JavaScript and must match Python exactly (tests/test_engines.py WebApp); the Scouting Lab changes anything, including the engine's thresholds, and shows each sentence's rule, the quiet rules and a diff. The battle engine (it needs Smogon's damage calculator) and the breeding engine's lineages come in as their last run; the Engine Room maps every engine's status and what's next (docs/APP.md)

decisions.title: The battle engine runs live in the app, every section of the scouting file with it.
decisions.text: The battle engine runs live in the app, every section of the scouting file with it. "Lets make that whole engine live including all the sections and how they get generated." The battle engine (engine.py, moves.py, knowledge.py, evaluate.py, trainer_policy.py, grid.py, scouting.py, playsheet.py, profile.py, phrases.py, scouting_report.py) is ported to JavaScript (app/web/27_battle.html) with Smogon's damage calculator (@smogon/calc 0.12.0, the same package the node bridge runs) loaded into the page. It must build the same Journey Scouting File as Python, number for number and sentence for sentence: every lineup, three edited ones and the what-if league, 2,365 sections (app/test_battle_parity.mjs; tests/test_engines.py runs three lineups). The Battle Lab (#/battlelab) edits members, builds, the coach's settings and the phrase book and regenerates every section with a diff, each sentence's rule and trigger, the quiet rules, and the fight behind every call turn by turn. Advance scouting builds each lineup live and checks it against the last Python run. The usage field's profile baseline stays a Python-computed cache; the lab never writes canon (variants go to the Variants tab or are copied as a lineups.json entry) (docs/APP.md)

decisions.title: The numbers decide, and the app has to work where it's deployed.
decisions.text: The numbers decide, and the app has to work where it's deployed. "I just want to make sure what is there is functional, and what is there runs on the engine that we've built that operates on the same principle that Pokémon itself does - which is that these numbers and stats and interactions determine everything." Every verdict the app shows must come from an engine reading the game's numbers (stats, typing, moves, abilities, items, the damage formula, the games' egg and learnset data); what isn't a mechanic is shown as what it is (your decisions, proposals, logged readings), never generated. So the matchup board on the scouting reports is now played out by the battle engine instead of read from type multipliers, and the Glasshouse instruments show only logged readings (the simulated readings D-055 allowed are gone). The deployed web app couldn't navigate: Apps Script's sandboxed frame turns a followed link into a blank page, so the app now routes clicks itself (google.script.history for the address and back button) and app/test_frame.mjs tests it in a frame built the same way (docs/APP.md)

decisions.title: Builds and names.
decisions.text: Builds and names. Ability belongs in the build ("yes ability belongs in the build"). Team-role tags are computed and can be overridden by hand ("yes exactly"): approved overrides go in engine/trainers/team_roles.json → overrides and both engines apply them (earned follows the override, the score stays computed, the read says so); the Pokémon lab tries them in the browser and copies them out for approval. Zack names everything: instead of asking, the engine lists everything that needs a name ("generate a list of all of the things that need to be named"): docs/naming/NAMES_NEEDED.md, 162 today (types, role nouns, hybrids, movesets, team roles, base-stat bands, team shapes, breeding lines, the unnamed word); until named they show as ⟨placeholders⟩. The 8 traits are the four sliders and their two ends

decisions.title: The four team roles.
decisions.text: The four team roles. Ace (Zack): beats at least 80% of its generation's Elite Four Pokémon and 70% of its Champions' one-on-one, both at level 100, in the battle engine ("let's leave it there for now"); the tier above Ace stays off until it has a rule. Wall and Support (Zack: "you pick the numbers and the thresholds"): Wall takes four or more hits from at least 60% of the 100 hardest-hitting Elite Four and Champion attacks against it, or both sides of its bulk sit in the top 20% of its generation; Support carries at least two support moves and its best support role in the role engine scores 0.40 or more. Sweeper: its best sweeping role in the role engine scores 0.60 or more. Rules live in engine/trainers/team_roles.json; distribution in docs/roles/ROLE_SCORES.md
decisions.who: Zack (Ace); assistant at Zack's request (Wall, Support, Sweeper)

decisions.title: Fight settings for the team roles.
decisions.text: Fight settings for the team roles. Both sides at level 100. A build with no recorded EVs fights with the standard 85 in every stat ("just do the standard 85"), and blank EVs never count as evidence for any role ("blank EVs just shouldn't affect anything"). Neutral means no type advantage either way, 1× ("just no type advantage")

decisions.title: Every rematch team counts, none skipped.
decisions.text: Every rematch team counts, none skipped. "I want all the rematch teams." FireRed's Elite Four and three Champion rematches, Platinum's Elite Four rematches, Crystal's rival (Silver) and his rematch, and HGSS's rematches all load with the game's AI flags, and the team roles read them

decisions.title: The four labs are built.
decisions.text: The four labs are built. "Just go ahead. Just run it." The Pokémon lab (#/pokemon: change moves, nature, ability, item, IVs and EVs and the four team roles, the build name, the scouting lines, the fit on your team and your measured trainer identity re-read live, before and after, with every rule and fight shown), build compare (#/compare/<species>: every build on record side by side), the team lab (#/team: six slots per game, default your journey six; type reads, the scenario questions, the team's shape, candidates with what each closes or opens, nature swaps), the breeding lab (#/lines: boutique lines offspring-first, with biology, abilities, the Pokédex, canon source, how each move gets into the egg and the crosses), PKHeX export on its own screen (#/pkhex), and the Scouting Lab as the Trainer lab. Records in three tiers (engine/store: species derived; builds and individuals stored with provenance yours, canonical, stock, ingested, competitive). Nothing in the labs writes canon (docs/design/FOUR_LABS.md, docs/APP.md)

decisions.title: The tier above Ace is "Joker"; Ace stays as it is.
decisions.text: The tier above Ace is "Joker"; Ace stays as it is. "thats fine for the amount of pokemon that earn ace - lets call that term above ace "joker" for now." Ace keeps its bar (456 of 962 builds earn it, with the cartridge teams fighting on no EVs). Joker is the name for the tier above it, well below Ash's Pikachu; it stays off until it has a rule (engine/trainers/team_roles.json → roles.ace.top_tier)

decisions.title: The master plan is the plan; build it on the existing framework.
decisions.text: The master plan is the plan; build it on the existing framework. "Okay this is the new plan. Use the old framework but build the new plan. Feel free to change the old plan" (docs/design/MASTER_PLAN.md, phases 0–8 in order). The existing engines, app, parity tests and rebuild stay the framework; earlier plans (FOUR_LABS.md and the master plan itself) may change as the build goes

decisions.title: Defaults taken for the master plan's four blocking questions, so the build could start
decisions.text: Defaults taken for the master plan's four blocking questions, so the build could start (each reversible; Zack may overturn any): Q1 the Ace score stays the plain mean of the two win rates and its note now says so (it decides nothing; Ace is earned on both bars); Q2 the unread `field_evs_each: 85` setting is removed and the Elite Four and Champions keep fighting on no EVs, the basis of the Ace count accepted in D-064 (D-061's 85 stays for our blank builds); Q3 the plan's storage split (reference and definitions in git; your records in append-only Sheet tabs My Pokémon / My Builds / My Teams; images in a Drive folder the app makes), read as approved by D-065, with D-025's "canon lives in the Sheet" read as "your data lives in the Sheet"; Q4 several of the same species in one game are allowed (ids get a token: docs/design/DATA_CONTRACT.md §2)

decisions.title: Breeding stock (Phase 4): the defaults it was built on
decisions.text: Breeding stock (Phase 4): the defaults it was built on (each reversible; Zack may overturn any): (a) Q10: a blueprint is a design, a build marked `kind: blueprint` in My Builds, and you can keep any number of them; D-038 still decides which animals actually live at the ranch; (b) "possible" means the hatch rules as the games' own code builds an egg (pret decompilations of Crystal, Emerald, FireRed and Platinum: the move order, the push-out, hatch level 5 in Gens 2-3 and 1 in Gen 4); the four-state verdict informs and decides nothing, learnability stays the gate (D-024, D-048); (c) a line's own male can be a link in a chain (hatched with some moves, learns the rest himself); (d) among equally short planned pedigrees, the studbook prefers a journey companion who can reach the game on cartridge (the same generation, or Gen 3 to 4 by Pal Park); a Crystal companion in a Gen 4 cross is still allowed, B29 stays your call; (e) "what a set might suggest" shows only evidence by kind (game mechanics, canon about the species) and draws no conclusion; an interpretation would be a hypothesis in the journal

evidence.text: Crystal and Platinum sixes have no Fly learner and no Waterfall learner; Platinum also has no Defog learner
HeartGold six covers all 8 HGSS HMs; all members and breeding sources obtainable in one HG save
Typhlosion Extrasensory is an HGSS-only Cyndaquil egg move → a legal Extrasensory Typhlosion isn't the Elm starter
Thunder Punch on Infernape (Platinum): tutor and egg both legal
Tyranitar Outrage obtainable from the HGSS tutor; Dragon Dance requires a 2-step egg chain
Mamoswine Ice Shard: Swinub Lv28 only in Gen 4; not relearnable after evolving
Swampert Refresh: Mudkip egg move; Milotic learns Refresh at Lv15 (legal father)
Mareep line not obtainable in Crystal except by trade
Growlithe absent from Emerald; FireRed-exclusive
No Sinnoh starters in HGSS → SoulSilver Infernape/Empoleon arrive by trade
Dragon's Den ExtremeSpeed Dratini not represented in either learnset dataset

v3 Copy of Canon Builds: column A was rewritten with the later rosters for every game (incl. sacred HeartGold, the former SoulSilver six and the rival six); columns B–P stayed in the original row order, so row *n*'s build belongs to Canon Builds row *n*
No Crystal, Platinum or HeartGold member can learn the missing field move (Crystal Fly/Waterfall, Platinum Fly/Defog/Waterfall, HG Flash) in any game ever, except Feraligatr–Waterfall (Gen 3+)
The Platinum Empoleon → Lucario swap removed the team's only Waterfall and Defog learner
Crystal's overworld Waterfall check only requires that a party member knows the move (+ Rising Badge), not species compatibility

Legacy legality formula: ⚠️ if any move isn't in that slot's MoveList, or there are duplicate moves, an empty slot, or no ability. Each slot reads its own MoveLists column (no shared-column bug). Breeding_Lab outputs are typed values, not formulas (computed by a script not visible anywhere)
Gen 2 stores no ball, nature, ability or PID (PKHeX GBPKM placeholders); gender and shininess derive from DVs; DV16 = Atk<<12 | Def<<8 | Spe<<4 | Spc
PKHeX Batch Editor syntax: .Prop=Value sets, =Prop=Value / !Prop=Value filter
Pre-Gen-6 base stats differ for canon species (Ampharos Def 75, Alakazam SpD 85, Roserade Def 55)
No companion in any of the six chapters has Flame Body or Magma Armor; fully evolved Gen 1–4 holders are Magcargo, Camerupt (Magma Armor) and Magmortar (Flame Body)
SoulSilver Scizor's Counter: Heracross learns it at Lv 25 in HGSS (Route 33, Azalea); Volbeat only via Emerald's tutor + Pal Park
Pikachu, HeartGold Pokédex: "roasts hard berries with electricity to make them tender enough to eat"; Magmar, HeartGold: "blows scorching flames to make the environment suitable for itself"
Gen 2 berries are the modern berries under old names (Berry = Oran, Gold Berry = Sitrus, MiracleBerry = Lum …); Lava Cookie and Old Gateau don't exist in Gen 2
Gen 4 hatch time = egg cycles × 255 steps (PokeAPI hatch_counter); Flame Body / Magma Armor in the party halves it. Larvitar 40 cycles (10,200 steps), the other eight stud lines 20–25
evidence.status: VERIFIED (PokeAPI; Gen 4 cycle length believed 255, verify)

evidence.text: Gen 4 berry growth: Lum Berry 48 h to harvest, Sitrus 32 h, the status-cure berries 12–16 h, up to 5 per plant
SoulSilver Pikachu (former set, no item) wins 5 of 32 benchmark 1v1s; with a Light Ball, 17 of 32
Larvitar can get Dragon Dance without leaving the journey: Dragonite (learns it) → Lapras (Water 1, then Monster) → Larvitar

The games' trainer AI (pret disassemblies). Gen 3–4 score every move from 100, highest wins: a knockout +4 (+6 with priority; Gen 4 checks the top roll, Gen 3 a random 85–100% roll); every attack but the hardest hit −1; a move that would fail −10; healing −8 whenever the AI isn't slower. Crystal scores from 20, lowest wins: a knockout −5, weaker attacks +1, healing −2 under 25% HP. Every Elite Four member and champion in the six games runs the same core flags: BASIC + EVAL_ATTACK + EXPERT in Gen 4 (HGSS bitmask 7), CHECK_BAD_MOVE + TRY_TO_FAINT + CHECK_VIABILITY in Gen 3 (Sidney and Lucian add SETUP_FIRST_TURN), and Crystal's seven layers for every boss class
evidence.status: VERIFIED (pret source, cited per entry in `engine/battle/trainer_ai.json`; HGSS per-move logic assumed to match Platinum)

evidence.text: Trainers use a Full Restore below 25% HP with no randomness in Gen 3–4. More item slots unlock as their party shrinks. Crystal uses items only on the highest-level Pokémon: never above 50% HP, always at 25% or less
FireRed's PREFER_STRONGEST_MOVE flag boosts status and fixed-damage moves, not the strongest attack. FireRed and Emerald swap the raw bit values of TRY_TO_FAINT and CHECK_VIABILITY

PokeAPI's move data misses some post-Gen IV changes that matter for Gen IV reads: Gen V's priority renumbering (Extreme Speed +1 → +2, Fake Out +1 → +3, Protect/Detect/Endure +3 → +4) has no move_changelog row, and move_meta_stat_changes holds only today's values (Growth's Attack boost, Tail Glow's third stage). Growth and Tail Glow are recovered from the rolled-back effect_id; the priorities are recorded as documented exceptions in engine/trainers/era_corrections.json
evidence.status: VERIFIED (PokeAPI tables; Gen V change list)

evidence.text: Showdown's public replay search (replay.pokemonshowdown.com/search.json) returns up to 51 replays a page, newest first, and pages back with before=<uploadtime>. Smogon tournament games appear in the same search under smogtours- ids, without a ladder rating. Replay JSON carries the full battle log in Showdown's protocol, with HP as percentages (the HP Percentage Mod)

Cartridge party order is the send-out order, and the ace is the unique top-level member: Lance (HGSS) Gyarados 46 → … → Dragonite 50 last; Cynthia (Platinum) Garchomp 62 last; Red (HGSS) Pikachu 88 leads
evidence.status: VERIFIED (pret data as loaded by the engine)

evidence.text: Bulbapedia's raw page source (index.php?title=…&action=raw) is reachable from the engine (Python's urllib passes; plain curl gets a Cloudflare challenge). A Pokémon's page holds the anime moves-used table as {{anmov|type|Move|EPISODE|Title|rec=yes}}; Pokémon without a page redirect to a {{TrainerPoké|pkmn=…|desc=…}} entry on the trainer page; Achievements list results as * [[Event]] - Result (''[[EP077|Title]]''). Gary's Indigo Plateau result is Top 32 (EP077); May's Kanto Grand Festival is Top 4 (AG182); Paul's Ninjask's known moves are Agility, Fury Cutter and Giga Drain (no Baton Pass)

Torterra's Pokédex: Diamond 'small Pokémon … gather on its unmoving back to begin building their nests'; Pearl 'groups … migrating in search of water have been mistaken for "moving forests"'; Platinum 'some Pokémon are born on a Torterra's back and spend their entire life there'; HGSS 'ancient people imagined that beneath the ground, a gigantic Torterra dwelled'

Smogon's monthly stats (smogon.com/stats/<month>/chaos/<format>-<cutoff>.json) publish gen4ou, gen3ou and gen2ou (and gen2uu) at cutoffs 0, 1500, 1630 and 1760. September 2026 gen4ou at 1630+: 57,675 battles, Tyranitar on 53% of teams, Jolly 252 Atk / 252 Spe its top spread (23%); checks and counters are {n, p, d}: matchups seen, the share ending with it knocked out or forced out, and its deviation

Bulk has to count HP. Physical bulk is HP × Defense: Snorlax (160 HP, 65 Def) sits above 82% of Gen 4's fully evolved field physically and 98% specially, Lapras above 83%, Blissey (255 HP, 10 Def) below 85% physically. Comparing Defense with Sp. Def alone tagged Snorlax, Lapras, Heracross, Togekiss and Milotic physically soft
evidence.status: VERIFIED (engine field pool, Smogon calc stats)

evidence.text: Gen I-II stats, the way Showdown and Smogon's calc read them: a DV is half the IV; the HP DV is built from the odd/even bits of the Attack, Defense, Speed and Special DVs; Sp. Atk and Sp. Def share one Special DV and one Special stat experience; stat experience (EV − 1)² + 1 adds the same quarter-EV as later EVs; no natures; and an open EV field means maxed stat experience. Light Ball doubles only Sp. Atk in Gen II-III (Attack too from Gen IV)

Showdown's protocol names an ability's owner by the line: on -heal … [from] ability: Volt Absorb|[of] p2a: Starmie (Water Absorb, Dry Skin) the healed Pokémon holds it and [of] is the attacker; on -damage/-status (Rough Skin, Static, Poison Point, Synchronize, Effect Spore) and -weather the [of] Pokémon holds it. -start|X|perish0 comes right before a Perish Song faint; -message|X lost due to inactivity. is a loss on the timer; a Ghost's Curse can knock out its user

PokeAPI's gaps for Gens II-IV: no event moves (Gen II's New York City Pokémon Center Eevee with Growth, Wooper with Belly Drum, Geodude with Rapid Spin, Nidoran♂ with Lovely Kiss, all on Bulbapedia's learnset pages); Rotom's form moves sit under each form's own id (method 10, form change); Gen II's berries are filed under their Gen III names (MiracleBerry as Lum Berry). Smogon's moveset files list a check only past 20 matchups and rank on the unrounded score (mean − 4 sd); read that way, our shares, raw counts, teammates and checks match Smogon's printed files for all 358 Gen 2-4 OU species at 1630+
evidence.status: VERIFIED (PokeAPI tables, Bulbapedia, smogon.com/stats moveset files, 2026-10-20)

questions.question: Which satellite: the Sevii Islands or the Battle Zone?
questions.why: Blackthorn has no volcano and no sea. Lapras needs the sea; both Infernape and the Infernape stud need volcanic ground. Either site covers both.
options: Sevii Islands (Kanto): Mt. Ember, the Ember Spa, the open sea, Lapras's home region
Battle Zone (Sinnoh): Stark Mountain, the sea, Infernape's home region, Platinum's villa

questions.question: Confirm the D-038 reading: one stud per target line, a male who knows the whole egg-move set.
questions.why: The whole studbook is built on it: 9 studs and one Light Ball. The other reading keeps the last father in each chain instead.
options: Yes: a stud of each target line
No: keep the last father of each chain

questions.question: Approve W-016 (Meganium, the Glasshouse gardener) and W-017 (Miltank, the nursery's milk)?
questions.why: Two of the Glasshouse's jobs are story-only until a world record backs them.
questions.blocks: two open jobs in the Glasshouse

questions.question: The Day-Care preserve: who gets invited, and what do clients' Pokémon experience there?
questions.why: It's the one open part of the ranch (D-040). Not urgent.

questions.question: The companions' genders.
questions.why: They decide who can father and who can mother. Until then every parent reads "could be". If HeartGold Tyranitar is male and knows Dragon Dance and Outrage, he's already the Tyranitar stud.
questions.blocks: who sires and who carries in every cross

questions.question: Which outside fathers become part of the story?
questions.why: Seven crosses borrow a father from outside the journey: Nuzleaf (Extrasensory), Kingdra (Dragon Dance), Muk (Disable), Heracross (Counter), Azumarill (Aqua Ring), Dewgong (Ice Shard) and Bellossom (Leaf Storm, Sleep Powder). Under D-038 they go home after.
